title: Throughput warranty playbook: contractual SLA definitions, error-budget math, and operational recovery
creator: Ava Morales
description: Draft a customer-facing throughput warranty playbook for Dedicated capacity that defines measurable SLA terms (availability and throughput), formulates a transparent error-budget and credit calculation, prescribes autoscale and failover behaviors, and supplies contractual language for sales/legal. Deliverables: legal appendix text, operational runbook, monitoring queries, and example customer notices.
acceptance_criteria: Clear SLA metric definitions with implementation-level query examples (production and synthetic checks)
Error-budget math documented with worked examples and credit payout formulae
Autoscale interlock rules and throttling policy for proportional degradation outlined
Legal-ready paragraph blocks (customer-facing and redlines) reviewed by legal
Runbook steps for detection, investigation, remediation, and customer communication created
Benchmarked measurement demo on staging that matches contract language
decision_log: 2025-02-24: Chose primary SLA metric = Tokens-Served Success Rate (TSSR) measured per AZ over a rolling 30d window with daily quantiles; reason: tokens aligns with billing and customer expectations

2025-02-26: Error budget defined as 100 - TSSR (percent) with graduated credit bands (>=99.9% = no credit, 99.0-99.9% = proportional credit, <99.0% = full remediation escalation). Chosen to balance customer guarantees with practical autoscale/backfill behavior
2025-02-28: Selected 99th-percentile latency SLO as secondary signal for performance credit triggers (to avoid crediting for transient tail latency spikes under load balancer churn)

2025-03-03: Contract language will include 'proportional credit' formula tied to shortfall in aggregated served-tokens vs committed throughput using sliding-window weighting to avoid single-day swings
2025-03-05: Decided to offer an optional 'burst protection' addendum (paid) that limits degradation during planned maintenance and supports pre-warmed spare capacity

worked_examples: Example A (single-AZ shortfall): Customer committed 1M tokens/hr. Over 30 days, aggregated shortfall = 5% -> credit = shortfall% * monthly fee * weighting factor 0.75 -> formula documented and computed in spreadsheet link

Example B (burst event): 6-hour outage with automatic failover to degraded model variant. Sliding-window adjusted shortfall counts half-weight for failover-period where degraded variant served >=50% capacity

Example C (latency-triggered credit): If 99th-p latency exceeds threshold for >=12 hours in a day and TSSR also drops, credit is proportional to latency-exposed tokens using latency-to-credit mapping table
operational_controls: Autoscale interlock: If projected queued tokens exceed 120% of committed throughput for >3m, trigger reserved-pool burst and notify customer ops
Degradation ladder: graceful degrade to quantized model variants by prioritized customer routes; per-route weights defined in customer entitlement table
Failover policy: cross-AZ redirect with warm standbys; failover window counts as degraded-serving unless warm standby fully matched capacity
Throttling policy: soft-throttle at 110% sustained load, hard-throttle at 150% sustained load; throttles must be logged and customer-aware (headers + dashboard)
Measurement cadence: TSSR computed hourly, rolled into daily aggregates and a 30d sliding window for contractual measurement
